title: Business statistics and probability with Python
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Describe data, use probability rules and distributions, sample and estimate with confidence intervals, test hypotheses, compare groups, fit simple and multiple regressions, and do it all in Python with business and financial data.

weeks.1: Describing data: center, spread and shape
weeks.5: Sampling distributions and the central limit theorem

blocks.deliverable: Summarize a year of daily returns in Python.
Model the number of defaults with a binomial distribution.
Build a confidence interval for a mean return.
Week 7 midterm; test whether two funds differ in average return.
Estimate a stock's beta with regression.
Check a regression's residuals and explain the problems.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Data study: with a supplied data set of stock and market returns, describe the data, test two hypotheses, estimate betas by regression for five stocks, check the assumptions, and write a short report with Python code and charts.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
